📌 Tehran, IRNA – Managing Director of the Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA), Hossein Jaberi-Ansari, has emphasized the need to explore opportunities for cooperation between IRNA and Cypriot media outlets and pave the way for expanding media relations.

During a meeting on Sunday with Mohsen Shamsizadeh, Iran's newly appointed ambassador to Cyprus, Jaberi-Ansari said that reports about the media situation in Cyprus could help identify potential opportunities for cooperation, adding that such reports would allow IRNA to evaluate possible areas of collaboration with media outlets in the country.
​
Referring to IRNA’s cooperation agreements with official news agencies in other countries, he said that if the necessary grounds for cooperation with Cypriot media outlets were available, an agreement could be drafted and implemented to expand such ties.
​
Jaberi-Ansari also announced that relevant news teams at IRNA were ready to cooperate with the Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in Cyprus to cover major developments in the country.
​
He highlighted the extensive network of Iran's diplomatic missions abroad and their professional expertise, stressing the importance of effectively utilizing newsletters and reports produced by these missions.
​
Referring to the limitations on deploying correspondents abroad, the IRNA chief stressed the need for cooperation between Iran’s diplomatic missions and IRNA to cover developments in their host countries, describing such cooperation as an opportunity to expand ties and establish direct communication channels between Iranian embassies and the news agency.
​
For his part, Shamsizadeh welcomed IRNA’s professional capabilities and emphasized the importance of facilitating the flow of information and strengthening media relations during his mission. He described such efforts as crucial for enhancing mutual understanding between Iran and Cyprus.
